# Real-world verification

Fixtures in `fixtures/` are hand-written: small, clean, and
optimistic. This file records what happened when the parsers met
**real** logs — from real runners on this machine, and from public
sample files. The real logs live in `fixtures-real/` and are covered
by `TestRealWorldFixtures` in `internal/reduce/reduce_test.go`.

## Logs generated by real runners (2026-11-08)

A small project was created in the cloud VM and run with the real
tools. Only the machine-specific path prefix was replaced with
`proj` so the fixtures are portable; the content is untouched.

| Kind | How it was made | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest` JSON | `python -m pytest --json-report --json-report-file=report.json --junitxml=junit.xml` on a 3-test file (1 pass, 1 `ZeroDivisionError`, 1 skip) | 1 finding, `test_math.py:5`, summary 3/1/1/0/1 — correct |
| `pytest` JUnit | same run, `junit.xml` | 1 finding, `test_math.py:5` — correct |
| `go-test` | `go test -json` on a tiny module with 1 failing + 1 passing test | 1 finding, `main_test.go:7` — correct |
| `tsc` | `tsc --noEmit` (TypeScript 7.0.2) on a file with a type error and an undefined name | 2 findings, `app.ts:1` (TS2322), `app.ts:2` (TS2304) — correct |
| `eslint` | `eslint --format json` (ESLint 10.14) on a `.js` file with `no-undef` / `no-unused-vars` | 3 findings, `app.js:1,2,3` — correct |
| `vitest` | `vitest run --reporter=json` on a 3-test file (1 pass, 2 fail) | 2 findings, `math.test.ts:4` and `:5` — correct, **via the stack-trace fallback** (see below) |

### Finding: real Vitest reports have no `location`

The official Vitest JSON example shows `location: {line, column}`
on each assertion result. The real run produced assertion results
with **no `location` field at all** (keys: `ancestorTitles,
benchmarks, duration, failureMessages, fullName, meta, status,
tags, title`). The file:line only exists inside the stack trace in
`failureMessages[0]` (`at /…/math.test.ts:4:42`). The parser now
falls back to that stack frame (ADR-6). Without the fallback, every
real Vitest finding would have had no file:line. The hand-written
fixture still carries `location` (it is valid input), but the real
fixture proves the fallback path.

### Finding: real ESLint needs a real config

A flat config that only listed `**/*.ts` rules produced 0 messages
for a `.js` file, and a `.ts` file without a TypeScript parser
produced a fatal parse error instead of real lint findings. The
working real run used `**/*.js` with `no-undef` (error) and
`no-unused-vars` (warn). Lesson recorded here so nobody "fixes" the
fixture by weakening the config: a config that matches no files
silently reports nothing.

## Public sample files (downloaded 2026-11-08)

| Kind | Source | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `trx` | `zyborg/dotnet-tests-report`, `trx-report/sample-test-results.trx` (48 tests, 1 failure) — https://github.com/zyborg/dotnet-tests-report | 1 finding, `…/PkiCertificateSigningRequestTests.cs:284`, summary 48/47/1/0/0 — correct, no parser change needed |
| `playwright` valid | `daun/playwright-report-summary`, `__tests__/__fixtures__/report-valid.json` — https://github.com/daun/playwright-report-summary | **Parser was wrong**: 12 findings, all with no file:line (see below) |
| `playwright` nested | same repo, `report-nested.json` (45 tests, all passing, deeply nested suites) | 0 findings, summary 45/45 — correct; proves nested suites and the all-green case |
| `pytest` sample | `numirias/pytest-json-report`, `sample_report.json` (10 tests) — https://github.com/numirias/pytest-json-report | **Parser was incomplete**: setup/teardown failures had no message and no line (see below) |

### Finding: the Playwright parser had the wrong field layout

The original parser read `results[].location` and emitted one
finding per failed **result**. The real format has no
`results[].location` — file:line lives on `error.location`,
`errors[0].location`, `errorLocation`, and the spec's `file`/`line`
— and one failing test has several failed results (retries). The
old parser therefore produced 12 findings for 2 failing tests, all
with empty file:line, and also emitted findings for a `flaky` test
that had passed on its last retry. Fixed in the parser rewrite
(see `docs/DECISIONS.md` ADR-5): one finding per `unexpected`
test from its last failed result, file:line from the error
location. After the fix the valid sample gives 2 findings, both at
`/project/tests/functional/add.spec.ts:10`, summary 14/11/2/0/1.

Sources for the real format: Playwright's own types
(`playwright@1.51 types/testReporter.d.ts`) and the Playwright
docs on JSON reporters (https://playwright.dev/docs/next/
test-reporters).

### Finding: pytest setup/teardown failures were invisible

The original parser only read `call.longrepr`. A test that fails
in a fixture has no `call.longrepr` — in the sample,
`test_fail_during_setup` and `test_fail_during_teardown` produced
findings with the placeholder message "Test failed: …" and line 0.
Fixed (ADR-7): read `longrepr` from `call`, then `setup`, then
`teardown`. After the fix the sample gives 5 findings with real
lines 17, 22, 32, 55, 70. The test item's `lineno` field (0-based
definition line) is now the fallback when the traceback gives no
line.

### TRX: no change needed

The real TRX sample confirmed the parser's assumptions: `Counters`
attributes, `Output/ErrorInfo/Message` + `StackTrace`, and stack
frames of the form `at … in <file>:line N`. It also confirmed there
is no `skipped` counter (skipped = `notExecuted`, ADR-8).

## What is still not covered by a real log

- A real Playwright run on this machine (Playwright needs a browser
  download; the public sample files cover the format instead).
- A real .NET `dotnet test --logger trx` run (no .NET SDK on this
  VM; the public TRX sample covers the format instead).
- A real-world log larger than 200 MB, and logs from CI systems
  (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps) with their own wrappers around
  these formats. The 200 MB test used a synthetic repetition of a
  fixture (see `docs/TESTING.md`).
